what_its_for: Sodium is an essential mineral your body needs to work properly. It helps control fluid balance, supports nerve and muscle function, and keeps your blood pressure stable. Sodium supplements or sodium chloride products may be given when your body loses too much sodium (a condition called hyponatremia), when you are dehydrated, when you have certain medical conditions like adrenal insufficiency or low blood pressure, or when you need nasal or wound irrigation. Your doctor may also recommend it if you sweat heavily due to exercise or heat.
how_to_take: How you take sodium depends on the form your doctor has prescribed: ORAL TABLETS or PACKETS: Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew unless the label says you can. Mix powder or packet forms completely in the amount of water shown on the label before drinking. NASAL SPRAY or DROPS: Gently blow your nose first. Tilt your head slightly and spray or place drops into each nostril as directed. Breathe in gently through your nose. Do not share your nasal spray with anyone else. IV (through a vein): This is given by a nurse or doctor in a hospital or clinic. You will not do this at home. Always take exactly as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. Do not take more than prescribed.
dosing: Doses vary widely depending on why you need sodium and what form you are taking. Typical adult oral supplement doses range from 1 gram (1,000 mg) to 2 grams per dose, taken 1 to 3 times a day with meals or as directed by your doctor. For general health, most adults need 1,500 to 2,300 mg of sodium per day from food and supplements combined. Children's doses are much smaller and based on age and weight. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take. Do not adjust your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store sodium tablets, packets, and oral supplements at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in a bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep all forms of sodium supplements tightly closed and out of reach of children and pets. Nasal sprays should be stored at room temperature and discarded after the expiration date. IV sodium solutions are stored and handled by your healthcare team.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking too much sodium, as this can raise your blood pressure and increase your risk of heart disease, stroke, and kidney problems. Avoid adding extra table salt to your food if your doctor has told you to limit sodium intake. Limit processed foods, canned soups, fast food, and salty snacks, which are very high in sodium. Avoid combining sodium supplements with other electrolyte products unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not use nasal sodium sprays that appear cloudy or discolored. If you have high blood pressure, heart failure, or kidney disease, do not increase your sodium intake without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet; sudden weight gain of more than 2 pounds in a day; shortness of breath or difficulty breathing; confusion, extreme weakness, or fainting; seizures; muscle cramps or spasms that are severe; nausea and vomiting that will not stop; very high or very low blood pressure; or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel your condition is not improving or is getting worse.
when_it_works: For oral sodium supplements used to treat low sodium levels or dehydration, you may start to feel better within a few hours to a couple of days as your sodium levels return to normal. Symptoms like muscle cramps, dizziness, and fatigue often improve as your levels stabilize. IV sodium given in the hospital works faster, usually within hours, and your medical team will monitor your blood levels closely. Nasal sodium sprays work quickly to moisturize and clear your nasal passages, usually within minutes of use.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Sodium is safe and necessary during pregnancy, but do not take high-dose supplements unless your doctor recommends it. Too much sodium can worsen swelling during pregnancy. BREASTFEEDING: Sodium passes into breast milk naturally. Supplementing with normal amounts is generally safe, but talk to your doctor before taking extra sodium. CHILDREN: Children require sodium but in smaller amounts than adults. Doses must be carefully calculated by a doctor based on the child's age and weight. Never give adult sodium supplement doses to a child. ELDERLY: Older adults are more sensitive to changes in sodium levels. They are at higher risk for both low sodium (hyponatremia) and high sodium (hypernatremia). Careful monitoring is important. KIDNEY DISEASE: If you have kidney problems, your kidneys may not be able to remove excess sodium properly. Talk to your doctor before taking any sodium supplements. HEART FAILURE or HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE: You may need to restrict sodium rather than supplement it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
